cards.meaning: supply cannot meet demand (a four-character economic idiom for a market shortfall)
cards.example: 三星这个季度的存储芯片就是典型的供不应求，需求远远超过了产能，所以利润才会暴涨这么多。
cards.examplePinyin: Sānxīng zhège jìdù de cúnchǔ xīnpiàn jiùshì diǎnxíng de gōng bù yìng qiú, xūqiú yuǎnyuǎn chāoguòle chǎnnéng, suǒyǐ lìrùn cái huì bàozhǎng zhème duō.
cards.exampleMeaning: Samsung's memory chips this quarter are a textbook case of supply falling short of demand — demand has so far outstripped capacity that profit exploded the way it did.
cards.note: 书面语/formal, a fixed four-character collocation common in financial reporting. Distinguish from the colloquial 不够 ('not enough'), which vaguely flags insufficient quantity — 供不应求 specifically names a market imbalance where demand exceeds supply, an economic concept rather than a simple shortage. Its opposite is 供过于求 (supply exceeding demand, overcapacity).
cards.tiesTo: Samsung's record Q2 chip profit (memory/HBM demand outstripping supply) set against Apple's supply-constrained guidance from the same shortage

cards.meaning: after all; when all is said and done (a connective giving the underlying reason that qualifies what preceded)
cards.example: 亚马逊上调了两百二十亿美元的资本支出预期，股价却不跌反涨，毕竟云业务的增长速度摆在那儿，投资人没什么好担心的。
cards.examplePinyin: Yàmǎxùn shàngtiáole liǎng bǎi èrshí yì měiyuán de zīběn zhīchū yùqī, gǔjià què bú diē fǎn zhǎng, bìjìng yúnyèwù de zēngzhǎng sùdù bǎi zài nàr, tóuzīrén méishénme hǎo dānxīn de.
cards.exampleMeaning: Amazon raised its capex guidance and the stock still rose rather than fell — after all, the cloud business's growth rate speaks for itself, so investors had nothing to worry about.
cards.note: 中性偏书面 / neutral-to-formal, common in both spoken usage and financial commentary. Distinguish from 到底, which is typically used in questions pressing for the real truth of a matter ('到底发生了什么' — what actually happened); 毕竟 isn't a question — it offers a convincing reason that acknowledges what was just said while emphasizing the more fundamental fact underneath it.
cards.tiesTo: Amazon's stock rising despite a $220B capex raise, because AWS's 37% growth justified it

cards.meaning: shortage; scarcity; deficiency in a specific item or supply
cards.example: Ang kakulangan sa memory chips ang dahilan kung bakit umangat nang husto ang kita ng Samsung ngayong quarter.
cards.exampleMeaning: The shortage in memory chips is the reason Samsung's earnings jumped so sharply this quarter.
cards.note: Neutral, everyday register. Distinguish from kakapusan (taught previously): kakapusan is more general, often used for money or day-to-day resources (e.g. a budget shortfall), while kakulangan fits better for a specific item or product whose supply isn't sufficient — a chip shortage, a labor shortage.

cards.meaning: fickle; ever-changing; volatile (general instability, no fixed direction)
cards.example: Pabago-bago talaga ang piso ngayong linggo — bumagsak, bumawi nang kaunti, tapos umuusad-usad na lang habang naghihintay ng datos ng implasyon sa Agosto 5.
cards.exampleMeaning: The peso has really been volatile this week — it dropped, clawed back a little, and now it's just drifting while the market waits on the August 5 inflation data.
cards.note: Neutral register, common in everyday and financial talk. Distinguish from umangat (taught previously), which names only a rise — one direction; pabago-bago describes a lack of overall stability, sometimes up, sometimes down, so it's used for a whole market or situation rather than one specific movement.
cards.tiesTo: The peso's choppy trading this week and oil-price volatility from the Hormuz standoff
